title: Affine descent of a perfect complex along a filtered colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] (the affine form of a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex]). Then there are an index $i$ and a bounded complex $P_i^\bullet$ of finite projective $A_i$-modules with an isomorphism $P_i^\bullet\otimes_{A_i}A\cong P^\bullet$ of complexes.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.18, Tag 0BC7, label more-algebra-lemma-colimit-perfect (the case A = colim A_i)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-finite-projective-graded-colimit-descent] to the underlying graded family P.X and the given bounds to obtain fixed bounded finite projective term models M at a stage i.

Each Mⁿ is finitely presented by Mathlib Module.finitePresentation_of_projective. Apply [lem-pc-affine-differential-colimit-descent] to these fixed models and the term isomorphisms. It returns j≥i, differentials on the scalar extensions of M, shape and square-zero equations, and compatible term isomorphisms.

Construct Q as a HomologicalComplex with these prescribed scalar-extended terms, returned differentials, shape, and square-zero proofs. Scalar extension preserves zero objects (Functor.map_isZero), finite generation (Module.Finite.base_change), and projectivity (Module.Projective.tensorProduct), proving all three term properties with the same bounds.
Use HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents on the returned compatible term isomorphisms to obtain the complex base-change isomorphism. Return Q and its three term properties.
